simple.meaning: שָׁחַר (shâchar) is a Hebrew action word meaning “to be dim or dark (in color).” BibleIQ anchors the English reading to this source verb before comparing its uses.
simple.biblicalBackground: This action appears 1 time in Job, beginning at Job 30:30. Its meaning becomes clearer as the uses are compared.
simple.inThisVerse: In this verse, the tapped English word is source-aligned to שָׁחַר (H7835) in the Hebrew text.
simple.whyItMatters: Actions in Scripture show what people do, what God does, and how covenant faithfulness or rebellion is described. BibleIQ compares the action across its occurrences.
simple.summary: שָׁחַר (shâchar) / H7835 is traced through Job 30:30 with source-language evidence and verse context.

definitions.full: H7835. shachar I. שָׁחַר verb be black (Late Hebrew שָׁחוֺר and derivatives, black, blackness , etc., Ecclus 25:17 Hiph`il make black ; Aramaic שְׁחַר (Jastrow Dalm), Aph`el grow black , so , coal ; Jäger BAS ii. 295 compare Assyrian šûru , coal , šurinnu , fire-pot ); — ׳שׁ , of skin Job 30:30 .
definitions.rootNote: a primitive root (identical with 7836 through the idea of the duskiness of early dawn);
